destination.name: Atherton Tablelands
destination.tagline: A volcanic plateau of crater lakes, giant fig trees and rainforest waterfalls
destination.description: The Atherton Tablelands is a plateau behind Cairns in Far North Queensland, built by volcanic activity over millions of years. Its crater lakes, Lake Eacham and Lake Barrine, are maar volcanoes, and remnant rainforest in national parks holds twelve bird species found only in the Tablelands and nearby ranges. Waterfalls such as Millaa Millaa Falls and Millstream Falls, strangler figs like the Curtain Fig Tree and the historic mining town of Herberton make good stops for a drive around the plateau.
whyVisit: See waterfalls tumble in the hills

goodToKnow.title: You need a car
goodToKnow.detail: Sights are spread across the plateau, which is reached from Cairns on State Route 52 or National Route 1. Yungaburra and Atherton have lodging.

goodToKnow.title: Bring binoculars
goodToKnow.detail: The Tablelands are an Important Bird Area, with golden and tooth-billed bowerbirds found only in the region and nearby ranges.

goodToKnow.title: Wet season rain
goodToKnow.detail: The wet season runs December to March, with heavy rain.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} is the drier part of the year, which makes the drives and walks easier.
